gaps.effect: With §45V in the list, 80% of the credit is kept out of the BEAT computation; without it the credit reduces regular tax in §59A(b)(1)(B) and returns dollar for dollar as base erosion minimum tax. The same plant electing §48(a)(15) (written by the same law) gets the listed §48 credit.
gaps.example: Modified taxable income $200,000,000 (10.5% = $21,000,000), regular tax $21,000,000, §45V credit $10,000,000: BEAT $10,000,000. Same amount as a §48 credit: BEAT $2,000,000.
gaps.dollars: $8,000,000 on the face; about $700,000 against the best alternative (sell the credit under §6418 at an assumed 7% discount), or nil while the §6417(d)(1)(B) cash election is available. Full loss for a BEAT-paying buyer of §45V credits.
gaps.could_cover: Nothing reads §45V in. Avoided by the §6417 cash payment, a §6418 sale, or the §48(a)(15) election. No 2022 credit was added to this list, which suggests it was left alone on purpose.
gaps.confidence: high that the words omit it; low that it is an oversight

gaps.effect: With §45V in the list an individual, trust or pass-through owner could use it against tentative minimum tax; without it the credit stops at tentative minimum tax. Corporations unaffected (§38(c)(6)(E)).
gaps.example: Individual, regular tax $1,000,000, tentative minimum tax $800,000, §45V credit $600,000: $200,000 allowed, $400,000 unused. If specified: limit $756,250, all $600,000 allowed.
gaps.dollars: $400,000 deferred, not lost (§39(a)(4) carryback 3 years, then carryforward). Against the best alternative (sell under §6418 at an assumed 7% discount, or the §6417 cash payment) about $28,000 or nil.
gaps.could_cover: §6417(d)(1)(B) cash election, §6418 sale, §48(a)(15) election (the §48 credit is specified, clause (x)). Frozen list: no 2022 credit added.
gaps.confidence: high that the words omit it; low that it is an oversight
